The problem, on your own listing

A 4.5 that is only just a 4.5.

This is the list Google shows next to Caza Beach. By the star counts on your listing, your average is 4.46. One more one-star review would show 4.4, level with Sanchia. Seaview Manor, 1.5 km away, shows 4.7. On Tripadvisor your guests give you 4.7. Google is behind because nobody asks them there.

Behind the score

Three leaks between a great stay and the next booking.

Sunday
Reception closed

Your site says reception is open weekdays to 19:00, Saturdays to 14:00, and closed on Sundays. The chat button on your website has a WhatsApp option, but it is switched off. A family planning December on a Sunday evening has a form and an email.

22
Reviews of three stars or fewer

Out of 162 on Google. They weigh on the average far more than a five-star lifts it. It takes about 90 more five-star reviews for Google to show 4.7.

Tripadvisor: 4.7 from 128
R2,093
A night, through Booking.com

What Google shows for tonight. Your own site offers rooms from R1,455 booked direct, but a guest has to go looking to find that out. A guest who books through a listing site stays the listing site's guest, and the next stay pays commission again.

Why it has to start now

December is your best review month of the year.

Seven rooms full of happy holiday families is the biggest batch of good reviews you will get all year. Asked at the right moment, a good share of them will leave one. Not asked, almost none do.

If review requests go live in January, December's guests are gone. So we start with reviews in week one, and do everything else around them.

How full are you for December already, and which months after it would you most like to fill?
